packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET 19 - UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING

Exposure / rule statement
No identification of the manuscript text or its author was present in my context before reading, and I make none. I opened only PROMPT.md and image-001..008 in this packet directory. One thing beyond the letter of the rules: I ran a file listing of the two packet directories named to me (to see the image filenames); that showed that packet.json exists but I did not open it. Note also that the overview image-001 shows a modern printed bookplate pasted on the board (text: "CASTILLA / IGNEM LUCEMQUE FERO / EX LIBRIS DR MARIE-PIERRE H. FERAUD-CASTILLA", engraver's signature small at the edge). That is an ownership mark of the host volume and says nothing about the fragment's text; I report it only because it is visible. I had already read packet 18 in the same session, which shows the same hand and layout (probably the same dismembered leaf or book); nothing in it named a work.

LAYOUT SURVEY (observation)
- image-001: overview, inside of a wooden board with leather turn-ins and the printed bookplate (rotated 90 degrees). Along the upper (spine-side) edge a horizontal parchment strip with script, upright in the image as supplied.
- Two columns separated by a blank intercolumn; a small rectangular parchment tab is pasted over the top of the intercolumn and another over the top line of each column near the sewing supports. Four lines per column survive; the top line of each column is trimmed/covered along its upper part, the fourth line stands just above the cut lower edge.
- No running title, rubric, coloured or enlarged initial, underlining or gloss visible. An enlarged (but ink, not coloured) capital S opens a sentence in the right column line 1 ("Swane"). Punctuation by punctus; one comma-like mark (punctus with a tail) after "wande" at the end of left column line 3.
- Script: formal book hand in brown ink, superscript abbreviation marks (d', uat', ab'), nasal bars, long s and round s, v with superscript o in "zv"(?). German vernacular word forms (observation only).
- image-005: overview of the second face, another board side with a parchment strip along the lower edge. The exposed strip is almost blank (reverse/glued face or abraded), but carries: (a) a small separate scrap pasted at the left with two lines of script (image-006); (b) a small scrap and a run of script along the very lower edge at the right (image-008), partly folded under and apparently upside down relative to the viewer.
- Tentative interpretation only: a horizontal slice through a two-column leaf; the columns are not continuous with each other on this strip.

AREAS SELECTED / UNREAD
Selected: all eight lines of face 1; the scraps on face 2. Unread: the covered parts of lines 1-2 of both columns; the edge text on face 2 beyond a few letters. Tiles: image-002 = left part of left column; image-003 = end of left column + start of right column (overlaps both); image-004 = rest of right column. Overlapping words given once.

TRANSCRIPTION - FACE 1 (images 002-004)

Left column (image-002 for line beginnings, image-003 for line ends)

image-002/003 line 1:  daz(?) [w?]erliche[n?] [covered by tab] g(?)esin(?) . e(?) des(?) niemen(?) vn(?) w[..]p(?)s(?)
image-002/003 line 2:  sich d' (d[er]) sun . e . e(?)[covered / abraded] d[.]s(?) [covered] [..]ertin(?) . h(?)
image-002/003 line 3:  habe uollinbracht uffiz ende din gebot . wande ,
image-002/003 line 4:  ich erlosit habe menſliche kūne (kunne) mit mim(?) blůte(?)

Notes, left column:
- line 1: the upper half of the letters is cut away or hidden; only lower parts are visible, so this line is low confidence throughout. "-erliche-" is fairly secure; "niemen" (or "niemer") and a following "vn" are probable; the line-end word has w, then minims, then descenders.
- line 2: "sich d' sun" is clear, then punctus, "e", punctus(?) and a letter before the surface is lost under white paper fibre. Toward the end "...ertin" (or "-ortin") and a final short sign.
- line 3: clear. "uollinbracht" written as one word (uollin bracht); "uffiz" with long s-like ff and tailed z.
- line 4: clear except the last word: I see b, a tall letter or superscript, then minims and a final stroke: "blůte" / "bůtn" / "blvtn". The word before it is three or four minims with m: "mim"/"mini" (min[em]?). "menſliche" has a mark above the first e/n; "kūne" has a bar over u.

Right column (image-003 for line beginnings, image-004 for the rest)

image-003/004 line 1:  sten . Swane(?) ein [covered by tab] [..] in(?) licht(?) d[..]e(?)[cut]
image-003/004 line 2:  darīne (darinne) so muz d' (d[er]) uat' (uat[er]) mīnin(?) sinn(?) sin . nicht mit
image-003/004 line 3:  [.]z . dāne (danne) als er wert ist . d' (d[er]) hochisten mīne (minne) zv mini(?) .
image-003/004 line 4:  wande er ab' (ab[er]) w'd(?) (w[ir]dic? / w[er]d?) ist d' (d[er]) hochisten mīne (minne) . so er got ist .

Notes, right column:
- line 1: "sten" ends a word begun in the lost line above. "Swane"/"Swanc" with large S; final letter e or c. After "ein" a pasted tab hides one word; after it the tops of letters are trimmed: "in", a word with l, tall letters and t ("licht"/"liecht"?), then a word beginning d.
- line 2: "mīnin sinn sin": three minim-heavy words. The first has a bar (mi[n]nin / minim?); the second begins with long s and has about five minims plus n (sinn / sunn / sinin); the third "sin" followed by a punctus. I cannot fix the minim count more closely. A superscript stroke/letter stands above "nicht" (the h has a tall ascender; possibly just the ascender).
- line 3: first letters "[.]z" or "iz"/"rz" at the column edge, then punctus. "wert" could be "wert"/"went"; r preferred. After "hochisten" a small hole/abrasion, then "mīne"; line ends "zv mini" with final punctus ("zv" has a superscript sign; "mini" = minims + i, perhaps "mini"/"mun"/"nimi").
- line 4: "w'd" - w with superscript sign followed by a letter like d or o with a superscript; then "ist". A black hole/blot sits between lines 3 and 4 above "mīne". "got ist" - small abrasion between "got" and "ist" but no letter seems lost.

TRANSCRIPTION - FACE 2 (images 006-008)

Scrap at left (image-006), separate small piece pasted on the strip:
image-006 line 1:  darr(?) allez(?) . z(?)[cut]      (possible alternative: "daz iz allez")
image-006 line 2:  [only tops of letters, partly under brown leather residue: h(?)...all(?)...]  [illegible]

Scrap and edge at right (image-008):
image-008 scrap:  mini(?) / mnm(?)   (four to six minims with one clearer m; lower part of a line, the rest folded)
image-008 lower edge, to the right of the scrap: a line of script folded under the edge and seen upside down or mirrored; I can make out roughly "...vppo[.] o(?) mit(?) un[..]..." but treat this as [illegible]; it should not be used for matching.
image-007: the strip is blank as exposed; faint set-off or show-through at lower right near the image-008 scrap, not readable.

LIMITATIONS
- Only four lines per column; top lines of both columns are trimmed and partly covered by tabs, second line of the left column is mostly lost under paper.
- Minim groups are ambiguous (no i-dots); readings marked (?) there are guesses at letter division, not at sense.
- Column order assumed left then right; text between the columns is not continuous on this strip.
- Face 2 gives almost nothing; the edge writing would need the strip lifted or imaged from the other side.
- Suggested further views: a tile of face 1 with the tabs lifted or under raking light; a rotated/flipped close-up of the lower right edge of face 2.
